entities.summary: The Gridley-class destroyers were a class of four 1500-ton destroyers in the United States Navy. Named for Charles Vernon Gridley, they were part of a series of USN destroyers limited to 1,500 tons standard displacement by the London Naval Treaty and built in the 1930s. The first two ships were laid down on 3 June 1935 and commissioned in 1937. The second two were laid down in March 1936 and commissioned in 1938. Based on the preceding Mahan-class destroyers with somewhat different machinery, they had the same hull but had only a single stack and mounted sixteen 21 inch (533 mm) torpedo tubes, an increase of four.

historicalSignificance.significanceNarrative: The Gridley-class destroyers played a significant role in the development of US naval capabilities during the interwar period, with their design influencing subsequent destroyer classes. They also contributed to the expansion of US naval presence globally.
